start.content: I am Hillel, a junior scribe assigned to the Court of the Gentiles. My hands are stained with the ink of market ledgers and the dust of Temple inspection records. You wish to understand the process?

choices.text: Tell me about the lamb market records.

market_records.content: Every family or group must have a lamb. The market records show the date of purchase. According to the Law in Exodus, the lamb must be selected on the tenth day of Nisan and kept until the fourteenth day. These ledgers track that.

inspection.content: For four days, the lamb is watched. It must be 'without blemish' (Exodus 12:5). The priests conduct a formal inspection to certify it is perfect and fit for sacrifice. No spot, no broken bone, no imperfection. It is a rigorous process.

choices.text: So a lamb is chosen, then inspected for four days?

connection.content: Precisely. Selected on the tenth day, inspected until the fourteenth. The anointing at Bethany... that was the tenth day of the month. And for the last four days, has He not been in the Temple, being publicly questioned and examined by every priest and scribe? They have found no fault in Him.

insight.content: The pattern is perfect. He is the Lamb. The records and the inspection... they are not about animal sacrifice anymore. They are about Him.

closing.content: Go. Look at your evidence again. You are not tracking a man; you are tracking the fulfillment of a 1,500-year-old law.
